claim: Appeals of a property-roll assessment to the county board of equalization must be filed by the end of the county's normal business hours on the fourth Monday of June.
cite: Idaho Code 63-501A. Taxpayer's right to appeal

claim: Appeals of an assessment on the subsequent property roll are due the fourth Monday of November; missed-roll appeals are due before the board adjourns at its January meeting.

claim: Filing an appeal does not suspend payment of property taxes pending the appeal.

cite: File an Appeal | Idaho Board of Tax Appeals

claim: Idaho property is assessed at 100% of market value less any exemptions.
cite: Understanding Property Taxes | Idaho State Tax Commission

claim: The homestead exemption is the first $125,000 of assessed market value of the homestead or 50% of market value, whichever is less.
The home must be owner-occupied and the owner's primary dwelling place; the owner certifies to the county assessor that no other homestead exemption is claimed.
An owner need apply only once if the owner still occupies the same homestead; the exemption is not prorated.

To receive the exemption for the current tax year, application must be made by the end of business on the last business day of the year; approved applications received after the second Monday in July are granted as tax cancellations.
After an owner's death the exemption continues for the year of death and the next tax year while the home remains part of the estate; the new owner must then reapply.
Claiming more than one homestead exemption triggers recovery of tax up to 7 years plus a penalty equal to the recovered tax on a first instance.
The separate Property Tax Reduction program can reduce property taxes by $250 to $1,500 on a home and up to one acre.
cite: Property Tax Reduction | Idaho State Tax Commission
